children: Fundstrat’s Tom Lee said on Friday that the immediate period in the market is a test of whether people want to be traders or investors, noting that there are “plenty of reasons to be optimistic long term.”

“If they’re investors, there’s plenty of reasons to be optimistic long term,” he said in an appearance on CNBC. “Valuations are there. We know that the U.S. has a huge lead on AI, and AI is incredible.” Looking out three, six, or 12 months, he added that “the risk-reward is incredible for stocks.”

Lee acknowledged that “markets are nervous about the near term,” but argued the longer-term setup remains favorable. He pointed to the current moment as potentially “the best entry point in the last 18 months to own stocks to expect double-digit gains.” He characterized the present weakness as markets “compressing all of these cumulative fears into the final weeks this year.”

Headlines involving “a political football around AI and finger-pointing around China and whether someone should be leading a company,” he said, are “scary, and it’s painful to sit through. But this is all noise in the picture of the next 12 months.”
Lee was referring to Nvidia, which witnessed the exit of its CEO, Jensen Huang, over allegations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese

, and his subsequent return as CEO earlier this week, sparking volatile movement in the tech sector. He pointed to historical patterns after elevated volatility readings and periods of high-yield weakness as supportive of better returns ahead.

U.S. stocks have endured a choppy November after peaking in early October. The S&P 500 has slipped roughly 5.5% over the last month amid sharp daily swings, including a steep drop to near 6,910 on November 20, followed by a strong rebound on November 23.
The more tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite, meanwhile, has dropped 9% over the past month, but is up 4% year-to-date.

title: Tom Lee Says Market Tests Traders Vs. Investors: Now Is the Best Time In 18 Months To Buy Stocks
